title: Union bound for a random restriction over a list of circuits
statement:
Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and consider a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction on $n$ variables, under which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and fixed to each of the two Boolean values with probability $(1-p)/2$. Let $c_1, \dots, c_m$ be a list of Boolean circuits on $n$ variables, and for each circuit $c$ let $\mathrm{bad}(c, \cdot)$ be a predicate on restrictions. Then the probability that some circuit in the list is bad is at most the sum of the individual probabilities:
\[
  \Pr_p\!\left[\exists\, i,\ \mathrm{bad}(c_i, \rho)\right] \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{m} \Pr_p\!\left[\mathrm{bad}(c_i, \rho)\right],
\]
where each term is the probability, under the same random restriction, that the corresponding predicate holds.
hypotheses_covered: a list of Boolean circuits on n variables
replaced:
